  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

According to recent reports, enzo Maresca ha rilasciato queste dichiarazioni nella conferenza stampa della vigilia dell sfida di Champions tra il suo Manchester City e il Napoli: “”Le parole di Allegri? Credo che in Italia siamo abbastanza bravi a piangere, è una partita importante tre punti valgono per noi come per il Napoli, mi aspetto un Napoli come l’ho visto con il Torino. Problemi nostri difensivi e di equilibrio? Dobbiamo trovare quanto fatto nelle prime gare ufficiali, difensivamente abbiamo concesso poco, nel Napoli ho visto una squadra di giocatori forti, hanno top player come McTominay, Hojlund, Olivera, c’è anche Lang è in forma, sarà una partita difficile. Se ci sono stati contatti in primavera con il Napoli? Sono felicissimo di essere qua, ci sono stati contatti con squadre italiane, ma non con il Napoli. Il Napoli attende ma propone anche, ha giocatori offensivi forti, giocare contro una squadra italiana è sempre difficile. In futuro tornare in Italia? Mai dire mai. Cosa c’è da cambiare nel calcio italiano? Bisogna essere un po’ più coraggiosi. Il Napoli come lo vedo? Vedo una squadra che sta bene, crea tanto e ha singoli importanti. De Bruyne? Posso solo dire che è un ragazzo spettacolare, top, nessun dubbio che, se contento anche fuori dal calcio, darà una grossa mano al Napoli”.

I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut. In a recent development, intervenuto in collegamento con Radio Mana Mana Sport, Riccardo Trevisani, giornalista, ha analizzato così il pareggio di ieri dell'Inter sul campo dell'Atalanta: "Succede che le problematiche restano le stesse di quando vai sotto 2-0: la squadra si distrae della propria grandezza e della propria forza. Ma questo può succederti se sei veramente forte forte 1-2 volte l'anno: qua succede 1-2 volte al mese e non è possibile.

Industry observers note that ho visto svarioni psicologici con Inzaghi, meno ovviamente, però ogni tanto si disunivano e facevano scivoloni pazzeschi: parto dalle 12 sconfitte nel 2023 ma va in finale di Champions. Come fa a fare 12 sconfitte in Serie A e fare la finale: vuol dire che va in distonia col cervello. Questa distonia prosegue anche con Chivu: la squadra gioca meravigliosamente bene e a volte si spegne.

Una parte del blocco Inter la vedo anche in Nazionale e alterna le stesse cose: mi sembra che il problema, più che accollarlo a Chivu e a Inzaghi, va accollato ai giocatori. Quando le va, le va e l'Inter non è giocabile: quando non le va non le va. L'Inter è consapevole di essere forte e perché ne è consapevole s'addorme: la Roma si convince di poter stare a quel livello e sta sempre a barra dritta. L'Inter mi ha molto deluso".

Bollettini medici che sorridono poco alle società di Serie B, perché dopo i casi di Empoli e SudTirol, anche dal Padova arrivano brutte notizie per quel che riguarda un tesserato, nello specifico Nicolas Galazzi, che durante la seduta di allenamento di venerdì 20 novembre ha rimediato una lesione inserzionale del tendine d’Achille della gamba destra, che rende necessaria l'operazione. Di seguito, il comunicato del club:.

In a recent development, "Il Calcio Padova comunica che l’infortunio occorso a Nicolas Galazzi durante la seduta di allenamento di venerdì 20 novembre si è rivelato più grave del previsto. Gli accertamenti clinico-strumentali eseguiti presso il Poliambulatorio Arcella hanno evidenziato una lesione inserzionale del tendine d’Achille della gamba destra, che rende necessario un intervento chirurgico.

Industry observers note that il calciatore sarà operato mercoledì 25 novembre a Torino dal dottor Matteo Guelfi. I tempi di recupero previsti sono compresi tra i 3 e i 5 mesi".

Il centrocampista ritrova Gattuso dopo la Nazionale: il 22 dicembre a San Siro affronterà la sua ex squadra.

Per Il Messaggero, l’amore di Davide Frattesi per la Lazio e la felicità di essere tornato a casa sono tali da rendere difficile immaginare che possa cedere a nuove tentazioni. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Il centrocampista nutre anche una stima sincera per Gattuso, che in Nazionale lo considerava unico e indispensabile.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Lo stesso giudizio su Frattesi era condiviso da Mancini. Con lui il centrocampista esordì in Nazionale contro la Germania il 4 giugno 2022.

Frattesi aveva bisogno di sentirsi importante, un numero uno e non un numero dodici: è così che, secondo il quotidiano, lo consideravano Simone Inzaghi e Chivu. Il prossimo obiettivo è conquistare la Supercoppa il 22 dicembre a San Siro, proprio contro l’Inter.

Moises Caicedo injury: Xabi Alonso makes worrying admission after Chelsea star's latest blow

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 22 Nov 2026 02:37, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 02:37.
  • Chelsea face an anxious wait to discover the full extent of Moises Caicedo's hip injury after the midfielder was forced off early during Saturday's 4-1 Premier League defeat to Leeds United.
  • The Ecuador international started the Stamford Bridge clash wearing the captain's armband before landing heavily in the first half after winning an aerial duel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 22 Nov 2026 02:37, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 02:37.

Chelsea face an anxious wait to discover the full extent of Moises Caicedo's hip injury after the midfielder was forced off early during Saturday's 4-1 Premier League defeat to Leeds United.

The Ecuador international started the Stamford Bridge clash wearing the captain's armband before landing heavily in the first half after winning an aerial duel.

Caicedo clutched his hip and initially attempted to play on before eventually making way for Jordan Henderson in the 22nd minute.

Rather than heading straight down the tunnel to the dressing room, the midfielder remained on the bench to watch his teammates capitulate after the interval.

Caicedo had already missed part of the current campaign with a calf concern and Xabi Alonso admitted after full-time that the club must wait to assess the severity of this latest setback.

Speaking following the heavy home loss, Alonso revealed that the midfielder was in noticeable discomfort and will undergo further evaluation on Sunday.

It has been revealed that "It's a knock and we need to wait until tomorrow to see how he is," Alonso stated via Sky Sports News. "He was in pain and let's see how bad it is.".

Chelsea had briefly moved ahead through Emmanuel Emegha's 25th-minute opener before Noah Okafor struck twice alongside goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson to seal a stunning rout for the visitors.

Alonso pinpointed the combination of Caicedo's premature departure and Leeds's rapid equaliser as the exact moment his side surrendered control of the contest.

"What went wrong was after their equaliser, after the change with Moi, we lost the momentum completely," the Spaniard added.

Industry observers note that "Until then we were doing okay. I think that we were creating, playing a lot on the pitch. We were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment, they started believing, we started not believing.".

Without Caicedo shielding the backline, Chelsea's midfield was repeatedly overrun as Romeo Lavia and Henderson struggled to contain Leeds's aggressive counter-attacks.

Alonso admitted his players never recovered their composure mentally and failed to threaten the opposition goal once the visitors seized the initiative.

The defeat compounds a frustrating spell for the Blues, who have now suffered back-to-back Premier League losses following their 1-0 reverse at Sunderland prior to the international break.

Alonso will be desperate to have his star midfielder available for Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest ahead of a demanding December schedule featuring home clashes against Crystal Palace and Liverpool.

Sources indicate that contro il Lecce è arrivato il quinto gol in campionato per Davide Frattesi con la maglia della Lazio. Il Messaggero in edicola oggi ha fatto il punto della situazione parlando anche del futuro del centrocampista ex Inter:.

"Scegliere la Lazio, in crisi tecnica ed economica, sembrava a tutti una follia eppure a lui è bastata una telefonata di Rino Gattuso, uno dei suoi ex ct, per capire che stava arrivando la svolta della sua carriera. Ripartire dal basso, è vero, ma con la certezza di diventare un giocatore importante per i compagni, i tifosi e lo stesso allenatore. «Io e lui siamo come due migliori amici, litighiamo spesso e facciamo pace, Rino mi chiede alcune piccole cose e io magari ne faccio altre» ha ricordato Davide dopo lo straordinario gol realizzato con un pallonetto da fuori area, di sinistro, contro il Lecce.

It has been revealed that non ha mai negato che Gattuso è stato decisivo per la sua scelta e non smentisce neanche che potrebbe essere l’uomo in grado di trattenerlo alla Lazio la prossima stagione, quando arriveranno offerte forse irresistibili sia per lui che per il club di Lotito. Che dovrà versare 10 milioni nelle casse dell’Inter, oltre ai 5 già spesi, per definire l’acquisto del centrocampista: un affare, considerando che per il suo cartellino la società nerazzurra (che mantiene comunque il 40% sulla futura rivendita) aveva investito quasi 40 milioni di euro.

It has been revealed that la sensazione è che Davide sia così felice di essere tornato a casa che nessuno sarà in grado di farlo cadere in tentazione. Troppo grande l’amore per la Lazio e molto sincera la stima per Gattuso, che in Nazionale lo considerava unico e indispensabile proprio come Mancini, con cui fece il suo esordio contro la Germania il 4 giugno del 2022. Lui aveva bisogno di sentirsi importante, un Numero Uno come merita e non un numero dodici come lo consideravano Simone Inzaghi e Chivu. Prossimo obiettivo: conquistare la Supercoppa a San Siro il 22 dicembre, proprio contro l’Inter".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 22 Nov 2026 02:59.

Arsenal face an anxious wait over the fitness of first-choice goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard suffered a shoulder injury during Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw at Newcastle United.

The 31-year-old looked in noticeable discomfort before being forced off in the 69th minute at St James' Park, leaving deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga to see out the closing stages.

Mikel Arteta's side had initially taken control through Eberechi Eze's first-half opener before quickfire strikes from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw turned the contest on its head after the interval.

Noni Madueke eventually struck a 78th-minute equaliser to rescue a share of the spoils and move the Gunners six points clear at the summit, yet Raya's premature exit overshadowed the comeback.

Speaking after the full-time whistle, Arteta viewed the result as two points dropped rather than one gained and admitted his goalkeeper's setback is a genuine concern.

"Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news," the Arsenal manager said via Arsenal Insider. "He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know.".

Raya's availability is now in serious doubt ahead of a pivotal week at the Emirates Stadium, with Arsenal hosting Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming title rivals Manchester City on November 29.

Should the scan confirm a spell on the sidelines, Arrizabalaga will be thrust into the starting lineup for two of the club's most demanding fixtures of the campaign.

The three-time Premier League Golden Glove winner has made 32, 38 and 37 league appearances across the past three seasons, and any lengthy absence could be detrimental, despite Arsenal's broader sturdiness out of possession.

Former Premier League midfielder Jamie Redknapp believes losing Raya for any extended period would represent a seismic blow to Arsenal's title defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports News, the pundit labelled the Spaniard the best goalkeeper in the English top flight and questioned whether his deputy can match those lofty standards.

"David Raya is the one player that is irreplaceable in that Arsenal team," Redknapp stated.

"Kepa Arrizabalaga is not up to the level of him – I think he struggles in the Premier League – he's now going to have to play some games. That's going to be difficult for him.".

Redknapp added that Raya's absence will change everything for the Gunners in the short term, leaving Arteta desperately hoping Sunday's scan delivers encouraging news.

Sarà oggetto di riflessione già da oggi ad Appiano Gentile, con il solito asterisco: il tempo per sistemare le cose, se non direttamente in campo, è ridotto al midollo. Mercoledì al Meazza arriverà lo Stoccarda in Champions League, prima del doppio impegno in tre giorni, tra sabato e martedì prossimo, contro il Genoa tra campionato e Coppa Italia. Gli allenamenti non saranno tantissimi, ma Chivu dovrà farseli bastare.

Industry observers note that anche perché certi problemi, tornati a galla ieri sera contro l'Atalanta, sono già noti a tutti in casa nerazzurra. L'atteggiamento molto spesso non riesce a essere quello giusto dal primo all'ultimo minuto. Dopo aver sofferto a lungo di mancanza di adeguata concentrazione all'inizio delle partite, la squadra nerazzurra ieri alla New Balance Arena si è ingiustificatamente sentita appagata prima del tempo e per più volte nell'arco della stessa gara. Il primo campanello d'allarme è suonato sullo 0-2, quando con troppa facilità la squadra ha concesso all'Atalanta di tornare in partita con il gol evitabile segnato da Elmas. La stessa cosa è successa anche nella ripresa, quando - non si capisce il perché - i Campioni d'Italia hanno evidentemente pensato di aver già vinto una sfida che ha presentato poi il conto quasi sul gong.

Legendary commentator MARTIN TYLER on taking the Premier League plunge in 1992, Arsene Wenger's fury, his love of Woking - and THAT Sergio Aguero moment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1423 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s new home or at least they will when everything is in order.
  • Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.

Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s new home or at least they will when everything is in order.

Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.

From wherever it ends up, it will project a moment in time when everything changed for Tyler, having walked away from a steady job at ITV and taken a leap of faith as lead commentator for the latest satellite channel.

'A new frontier,' admits Tyler, the undisputed ‘Voice of the Premier League’ by the time he left the role at Sky, more than 30 years later.

'We didn’t know where it would take us, so that was a special day. Feeling a bit like a pioneer. Wondering whether we were all on a fool’s errand. Some people turned down the job I accepted because of the risk. My kids were four and two at the time.

'We used to travel to the games by train in those days, and we would look out of the window and count the satellite dishes as we passed through a substantial town. We didn’t know whether it was going to work. I wasn’t sure anybody would be watching.

Legendary football commentator Martin Tyler has released a book: TALES FROM THE GANTRY.

Tyler was the undoubted 'Voice of the Premier League' by the time he left Sky Sports in 2023.

Sources indicate that 'It was slow off the ground and there was a feeling within the game against live football, that people wouldn’t go to the games if they were televised live, and it ended up the opposite. Attendances have gone up, an amazing paradox. Now you can’t get a ticket.'.

Televised football has come a long way since Tyler’s first commentary game, Southampton v Sheffield Wednesday in the old Division Two in 1974, shot with just four cameras for Southern Television.

'Now if you don’t have 24 cameras you can feel a bit short-changed,' he laughs. 'I worked at ITV for about 17 years, most of it commentating and you would get a crew on match day who had been doing Coronation Street or Emmerdale Farm in the week and a match director from light entertainment.'.

The Premier League has come a long way, too. Some might argue too far. It has led football from its roots as the working man’s game to a place where clubs are owned by nations states and mired in the legal complications of the Manchester City case.

Tyler wants to reserve comment on City’s financial offences until sentencing is passed, aware he is inextricably bound to their success because of his iconic commentary for Sergio Aguero’s winner in the 93rd minute against Queen’s Park Rangers to snatch the Premier League title from Manchester United in 2012.

'I’ve always mentioned you won’t see anything like it again, and I stick to that,' he claims, although he the 'Aguero moment’ as it has become commonly known probably means less to him than it does to others.

He is proud to deliver the words but insists those moments belong to the players, the clubs and the fans, not to him.

Ask about his favourite game from three decades in the Premier League and Tyler instinctively pulls Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win against Newcastle in 1996 from the thrillers he has called.

His own footballing background, meanwhile, could hardly be any further from the Premier League’s glitzy, moneyed elite.

Sources indicate that tyler has always supported Woking and played as an amateur for Corinthian-Casuals. 'The law was you couldn’t get paid,' he says. 'We were on expenses only and they weren’t dodgy expenses. If I went on the tube to Leytonstone, I got the tube fare repaid and no more.

'I played for five years at that level and never got a penny because that was the rule. I played my last game in 1973 and within two years’ they got rid of it because so many people were bending the rules. An opposition player told me their team were on £75 a game.'.

Tyler reflected on his time in the game as a player, coach and commentator with Daily Mail Sport's Matt Barlow.

He was famously on commentary for Sergio Aguero's title-winning moment in 2012.

From a cricketing family, Tyler was on the books at Surrey where he twice served as 12th man and lived for a time with Bob Willis, who became one of England’s greatest fast bowlers after moving on to Warwickshire.

His manager for a time at Casuals was Surrey legend Micky Stewart, who had also played for the famous amateur football club before turning professional at Charlton. In those days it was possible for the multi-talented to hold down a decent career in two sports.

An afternoon in Tyler’s manufacturer is just as likely to involve digressions into non-league football, where he worked as an assistant to Alan Dowson at clubs including Woking and Hampton & Richmond, as it is into the Premier League.

He might regale you with a story about Arsene Wenger and the time, on the way to the gantry at Wigan Athletic, he slipped deeper than he realised into long conversation with the then Arsenal boss about rioting in Paris and almost missed his pre-match slot.

And he might pivot from there into Wenger’s fierce rivalry with Sir Alex Ferguson. 'I have seen Arsene very, very grumpy,' says Tyler. 'When he lost the FA Cup semi-final when Dennis Bergkamp missed the penalty and Ryan Giggs scored.

'I have never seen a manager so angry because he knew he had handed over not only an FA Cup final place but also the domination they enjoyed at that time. They had done the Double in 98 and he felt that was not only about losing a match but losing their psychological edge over their greatest rivals. He was livid. Talk about winning and losing with dignity.'.

But there’s every chance he will reminisce about the time when, as a schoolboy Woking supporter in the terrible winter of 1962-63 he was rewarded for volunteering to paint the stands with an invitation to travel on the team bus to an Amateur Cup tie at Lydbrook Athletic.

It has been revealed that 'We left Woking at seven on the morning of the match for a two o’clock kick-off in Gloucestershire and by nine we were digging the bus out of a snowdrift on the A4,' states Tyler. 'We got there at four, no floodlights, and they had marked the lines on the snow with blue soap powder but there was no way we could play. We turned around to go back, got stuck in Cheltenham and had to stay for the night.'.

The only other footballing image on display in Tyler’s home is a photograph of him and Dowson celebrating as the final whistle confirmed their Hampton & Richmond side as Isthmian League champions in 2016.

Tyler has had a hugely varied career, all the way from grassroots level right to the top.

Tyler even worked as an assistant coach to Alan Dowson at several Non-League clubs.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

After collecting the trophy, Tyler jumped into his car, drove north and less than 24 hours later was at the King Power Stadium to see Leicester crowned champions of England.

'The greatest fairytale story in the Premier League,' as he says. 'I had sampled that in a tiny non-league way, then taken those feelings with me to Leicester where it was multiplied a million times, but I could tell the world a tiny bit about how wonderful they must be feeling.'.

Industry observers note that the range of his experience is vast. From amateur football in the 60s, through regional television and ITV to Sky’s Premier League revolution. He commentates regularly and coaches at Woking’s academy and has written a book.

It is a wonderful compilation of 110 essays, the reflections on his lifetime in football. 'The random thoughts of a football obsessive,' as he likes to call it.

Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr has confirmed that he is in discussions over a latest contract at Selhurst Park after putting Liverpool's summer transfer interest behind him.

The 28-year-old Senegal international was keen on a switch to Anfield before the Eagles reportedly rejected a £50m offer from the Merseyside giants.

Liverpool had been assessing alternatives to primary target Bradley Barcola before eventually meeting Paris Saint-Germain's £123m asking price.

Despite the frustration of seeing a high-profile move collapse, Sarr insists he remains settled in South London and is open to agreeing improved terms on his current deal that runs until 2029.

Speaking to BBC Sport, the former Watford attacker admitted he naturally gave serious thought to what joining one of world football's biggest clubs would mean for his career.

However, Sarr stressed that he is no longer dwelling on the past and is solely focused on returning from a groin injury that has restricted him to just two Premier League substitute appearances this term.

Sources indicate that "Today, that chapter is behind me," Sarr mentioned. "I've always believed that you can't move forward if you're constantly looking in the rear-view mirror.".

Recent findings suggest that addressing his long-term future with the club, the winger confirmed: "Yes, there have been discussions with the club. For now, I prefer to let those conversations happen privately and concentrate on football.".

Sarr netted 21 goals across all competitions last season to help Palace lift the Conference League trophy and the board are keen to reward his stature in the squad.

When Sarr completes his recovery, he will return to work under latest head coach Thomas Frank following the dismissal of Pierre Sage.

The former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur manager endured a chastening start to his tenure on Saturday as a late Dwight McNeil own goal condemned Palace to a 3-2 defeat at Coventry City.

That setback stretched the Eagles' dismal run to five consecutive Premier League losses, leaving them mired in an unexpected early relegation battle.

Nevertheless, Sarr remains adamant that the dressing room possesses the quality and collective resilience required to spark a turnaround under Frank's fresh approach.

Industry observers note that "We all have to take responsibility, work together and fight for every point," Sarr added. "I'm confident we can overcome this difficult period and achieve our objectives this season.".

Palace host Real Sociedad in the Europa League on Thursday before welcoming Hull City to Selhurst Park for Frank's home bow in charge of the Eagles.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervenuti su Youtube, Gianpaolo Calvarese e Piero Giacomelli hanno commentato il rigore dato all'Inter contro l'Atalanta.

Calvarese: "Tanti episodi per Maresca che ha fatto bene, alcuni episodi davvero complessi dal punto di vista regolamentare".

Giacomelli: "Mi è piaciuto l'atteggiamento, in certe cose mi rivedo, la calma, la tranquillità. Mi piace da morire chi riesce ad essere calmo in campo, nelle fasi finali del match lo è stato".

Sources indicate that calvarese: "Grande personalità, anche se ogni tanto esagera ma devo dire che si è messo un po' in linea, quando sta bene è imbattibile. Il primo calcio di rigore è strano, Zappacosta si appoggia a terra con un movimento naturale, secondo me il primo braccio non è punibile ma c'è un extra movimento, non voglio sapere se istintivo o volontario, ma quel movimento è punibile".

Giacomelli: "Su questo ci sono pochi dubbi, il movimento è innaturale e punibile, si accorge di aver fatto una frittata, Zappacosta avrebbe preferito prendere un rosso perché per un difensore prendere giallo significa che quella palla non sarebbe entrata in porta, cosa che invece le immagini testimoniano. Dal punto di vista calcistico, il calciatore è contento di aver preso il giallo ma pensa che l'arbitro l'abbia reputata, secondo me in maniera corretta, una palla che non stava entrando".

It has been revealed that calvarese: "C'è una certezza: quel movimento fa sì che il VAR avalli la decisione. Non so se Maresca abbia fischiato il primo o il secondo movimento, mi rimane il dubbio. Ma sono convinto che il secondo movimento abbia levato ogni dubbio al VAR che quindi non è intervenuto".

Giacomelli: "Maresca è messo talmente bene che vede bene, noi vediamo la main, lui ha una reverse, il secondo movimento lo vede meglio di sicuro e per lui è molto più semplice di quanto non lo sia in TV".

Calvarese: "Non è cartellino rosso in ogni caso, fughiamo ogni dubbio perché ho sentito tanti che chiedevano il rosso".

Il Napoli ha messo gli occhi su Alessio Cacciamani. Dopo i tentativi di Roma e Milan durante la scorsa estate, il club partenopeo può andare alla carica per il giovane esterno del Torino, diventato una delle rivelazioni più interessanti di questo inizio di stagione. Il classe 2007 sta convincendo tutti con la maglia granata e il suo rendimento ha inevitabilmente fatto lievitare la valutazione del cartellino. Adesso, per convincere Urbano Cairo a sedersi al tavolo delle trattative, potrebbero servire circa 30 milioni di euro.

According to recent reports, quest'estate i granata hanno scelto di puntare sul ragazzo, respingendo le avance di vari club e inserendolo stabilmente nel progetto della prima squadra. Una decisione che, almeno finora, sta dando i suoi frutti. Cacciamani ha conquistato spazio e fiducia, diventando un elemento importante nelle rotazioni di Ignazio Abate. La Roma continua a seguirlo e potrebbe ripresentarsi in futuro, ma dovrà fare i conti con una richiesta economica decisamente più alta rispetto a quella della scorsa estate.

In campionato ha già collezionato 10 presenze, nove delle quali da titolare, per un totale di 746 minuti giocati. A questi si aggiunge un assist. Nato il 29 giugno 2007, Cacciamani ha ancora ampi margini di miglioramento. La valutazione vale è di circa 30 milioni.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 06:36.

Liverpool defender Kostas Tsimikas is reportedly expected to leave the club at the end of the season.

Tsimikas became only the second Greek player to represent the Reds when he joined the club in the summer of 2020, having been signed by then-manager Jurgen Klopp.

The 30-year-old has made 124 appearances for Liverpool across all competitions but has never been able to establish himself as a regular starter.

Tsimikas spent last season on loan at AS Roma before returning to his parent club in the summer, where he has once again found himself playing second fiddle to Milos Kerkez.

The left-back has made just one start in the Premier League this season, with a further three appearances coming off the bench as Kerkez has enjoyed the majority of opportunities.

However, Tsimikas has featured more regularly in cup competitions, making three Champions League starts this season and one appearance in the EFL Cup.

According to Greek journalist Ilias Kallonas of Sport24, Tsimikas to expected to leave Liverpool after the end of the current campaign.

The defender's contract at Anfield expires at the end of the season, and there is reportedly little to no chance of him being offered a new deal.

With Tsimikas seemingly destined to leave Liverpool, it will be interesting to see how the club approach the transfer market in their search for a replacement.

The Reds could target an established Premier League left-back to provide competition for Kerkez, or they may opt to invest in a younger player with considerable potential.

It has been reported that Liverpool and Arsenal are tracking New England Revolution defender Peyton Miller, who could be in line for an eye-catching move to a major European club in the future.

Scouts from Chelsea and both Manchester clubs have also been regular visitors to watch the youngster, who is under a long-term contract with the Revolution until 2030.

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 07:07.

Manchester United are reportedly set to be without Marcus Rashford for their upcoming Premier League showdown against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

The Red Devils head into one of English football's fiercest fixtures sitting 18th in the Premier League table, with Mauricio Pochettino preparing to take charge of his first game since replacing the sacked Michael Carrick.

The Argentine faces a daunting introduction to life at Old Trafford, having won just three of his previous 19 managerial encounters with Liverpool.

Rashford has been reintegrated into the Manchester United squad after Barcelona opted against making his loan move permanent.

The England international has made six Premier League appearances this season but is yet to find the net or register an assist, leaving him short of the influence expected from a player of his calibre.

The 29-year-old featured in United's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, but has reportedly been struggling with a hip problem ever since.

According to the Evening Standard, Rashford had been hoping to recover in time for Sunday's showdown, but he is now expected to miss the trip to Anfield, dealing Pochettino another setback ahead of his managerial debut.

Pochettino is also expected to be without several other vital players, with Carlos Baleba, Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte still sidelined ahead of Sunday's contest.

Left-back Luke Shaw remains unavailable, while goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also been contending with an injury.

There is some encouraging news for the fresh United boss, however, with Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu returning to training and expected to be included in the matchday squad, while Lisandro Martinez is also back in contention after serving his suspension.

Meanwhile, Andoni Iraola has received a timely quadruple boost, with Dominik Szoboszlai, Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all expected to be available after overcoming fitness concerns.

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have also returned to training, although neither is expected to feature against United, while Hugo Ekitike remains unavailable.

Lionesses and Arsenal star Chloe Kelly stole the show at the GQ Men of the Year Awards on Tuesday night, going braless in a see-through dress just hours after missing out on Sarina Wiegman's latest England squad.

Industry observers note that the two-time Euros and Champions League winner arrived on the red carpet in a long-flowing navy dress, showing off her toned body and glamorous long blonde hair. She was joined by former England stars Mary Earps and Alex Scott.

Kelly was once again left out of Wiegman's selection for the play-offs against Ukraine due to a hamstring injury, as the winger's battle to make the plane for next summer's World Cup continues.

Wiegman confirmed her squad on Tuesday morning, turning to England's younger generation for the double-header against Ukraine.

Izzy Goodwin is the latest emerging talent to receive a call-up to the Lionesses squad, after Lexi Potter, Erica Meg Parkinson and Freya Godfrey won their first caps in the previous round against Greece.

The 23-year-old London City Lionesses striker scored the equaliser against Kelly's Arsenal last weekend at the Emirates, with the home side dropping points yet again.

Chloe Kelly looked glamorous in a long-flowing navy dress at GQ Men of the Year 2026.

The 27-year-old missed out on Wiegman's England squad for the second time in a row.

Arsenal have had an underwhelming start to the season, with just three wins in 10 games, and they right now sit in sixth place in the WSL table.

Kelly was dropped for the first time by Wiegman for the previous qualifiers against Greece, alongside fellow forward Ella Toone.

'The main reason is that I think the levels weren't what I expect from them on the pitch,' Wiegman explained at the time.

Toone has returned to the latest squad, with Wiegman praising her reaction to being dropped last time out.

Sources indicate that 'She responded really well (to being dropped last camp),' Wiegman said: 'Working really hard, she came in and was ready straight away. Going back to club she's done well and that's what has been fed back to me, too.'.

As for Kelly, however, it has since been confirmed that she has been struggling with a hamstring injury which has kept her from competitive first-team action since the end of September.

The winger has started just one game for Arsenal, a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace, and has not registered any goals or assists. She has yet to complete 90 minutes in the WSL this season.

She was previously omitted from Wiegman's squad in 2025 for a lack of playing time as she fought with Mary Fowler for minutes - a disappointment that inspired her move to London from Manchester City.

Kelly was joined by former Arsenal and England legend Alex Scott.

Kelly has been battling a hamstring injury that has plagued her since the end of September.

Known for showing up in massive moments, it was a gamble that paid off and Kelly scored the winning penalty against Spain to win Euros 2025, earning her the nickname Chloe 'clutch' Kelly.

Now, she faces fierce competition from fresh German signing Lisa Baum, with other talented wingers Caitlin Foord and Olivia Smith refusing to roll over.

Kelly will have to steal the spotlight yet again to get a glimpse of Wiegman's England side.

Secondo successo per l'Italia, che continua il suo percorso nel Mondiale Under 17: Costa d'Avorio battuta con un gol per tempo, con gli Azzurrini di Franceschini che dominano il campo soprattutto nel primo tempo e rischiano poco anche nella ripresa. Queste le note migliori e peggiori della sfida appena terminata in Qatar:.

L'Atalanta regna - Perillo di punta, Fugazzola poco dietro, e le due mezzali Olivieri (2010) e Gasparello: proprio dai due centrocampisti arrivano i gol che decidono la partita e in generale gli episodi che indirizzano la partita nella direzione azzurra. Anche la presenza di quattro orobici nella formazione titolare dice tanto su quanto la Dea conti nella rosa a disposizione di Franceschini.

Il muro Djibril Diallo - Seconda gara di fila e seconda prova da incorniciare per il centrale del Parma, che ha acquisito una consapevolezza nei propri mezzi superlativa e lo si vede bene in campo, dove svetta sugli avversari senza preoccuparsi della fisicità mostrata dagli africani. In questo momento è uno dei titolarissimi di Franceschini, vediamo se contro l'Uzbekistan gli verrà dato un turno di riposo.

Il rigore finale - Leggerezza che si poteva evitare anche solo capendo lo stile arbitrale molto incline all'uso del VAR da parte dell'arbitro Michael Venne: Varali interviene in scivolata e tocca in modo lieve ma sicuramente percettibile l'avversario. La qualificazione al momento non è minimamente in dubbio, ma la differenza reti è un dato importante e regalare il rigore in pieno recupero è un errore da cui imparare in vista delle prossime gare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervenuti su Youtube, Gianpaolo Calvarese e Piero Giacomelli, ex arbitri, hanno commentato la scelta di Maresca di dare rigore all'Atalanta per il tocco di braccio di Bastoni nel finale di Atalanta-Inter.

Industry observers note that giacomelli: "Secondo me Maresca ha un po' di fortuna, era andato largo in una posizione che abitualmente non teniamo, secondo me è andato dietro a De Ketelaere pensando che avrebbe puntato l'uomo. La palla si impenna e poi è messo bene Maresca e vede queste braccia che sono davvero tanto larghe, un aumento ingiustificato. La tranquillità e la calma con la quale ha dato rigore porta a pensare che lui ha visto questo, da dov'era posizionato lui lo si vede meglio rispetto alle telecamere. Quando guardi la prima immagini dici: 'pff, cos'è successo?'. Poi riguardi il replay e vedi che Bastoni ha le braccia tanto in alto e non sembrano andare a coordinarsi, sembra un aumento più ingiustificato, è questo quello che ha visto Maresca".

In a recent development, calvarese: "Le braccia sono tanto in alto, quel movimento delle braccia di Bastoni sia innaturale, non giustifica lo slancio di voler prendere il pallone di testa. Sono per il calcio di rigore e se non lo avesse concesso dal campo il VAR sarebbe intervenuto, il movimento è innaturale".

Giacomelli: "Il movimento del braccio non è funzionale per staccare, sono capitate altre situazioni nelle quali il difensore tenta di saltare e impatta, Bastoni ha alzato entrambe le braccia, la vedo come Maresca. Tanta roba perché era messo bene".

Calvarese: "Prendere due rigori non è semplice, una partita difficile, combattuta fino alla fine, Maresca è stato bravo".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 07:39.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly set to go head-to-head in the race to sign Freiburg forward Igor Matanovic during the January transfer window.

The 23-year-old joined Freiburg in the summer of 2025 and has since made 64 appearances across all competitions for the Bundesliga outfit.

The Croatian enjoyed an impressive campaign last season, registering 15 goals in all competitions, and has already found the net eight times in 2026-27, including five strikes in the Bundesliga.

Man Utd have been linked with a move for Matanovic in recent weeks, although Arsenal and Chelsea are also understood to be monitoring his situation.

According to a fresh report from iNews, Tottenham have now joined the pursuit of Matanovic, with Roberto De Zerbi keen to bolster his attacking options ahead of the second half of the campaign.

Man Utd are also reportedly firmly in the running for the Croatian international, although Freiburg are expected to demand a fee in the region of £50m before sanctioning his departure.

Spurs, meanwhile, could make room for a latest centre-forward by offloading Richarlison in January, with the club reportedly prepared to accept an offer of around £10m as Turkish outfit Trabzonspor continue to retain an interest in the Brazilian.

Pochettino would also welcome the arrival of another forward to provide competition and support for Benjamin Sesko, particularly with Joshua Zirkzee potentially heading for the exit after managing just 89 minutes of Premier League action this season.

Although Matanovic is understood to have attracted interest from clubs in other leagues, reports suggest that the Freiburg striker would favour a move to the Premier League should the opportunity arise.

After enduring a nightmare start to the campaign, De Zerbi's side have shown signs of a considerable revival and have climbed to ninth in the Premier League table, giving the Italian some encouragement ahead of the January window.

Strengthening the centre-forward department remains a priority for Spurs, who have also been linked with Bournemouth youngster Eli Junior Kroupi, although they could face stiff competition from Liverpool, Arsenal and Barcelona for his signature.

Endrick is another name who could attract interest from Premier League clubs after struggling to make a significant impression under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid, although any potential move is more likely to materialise in the form of a loan deal.

La vendita per i tifosi ospiti resta sospesa in attesa della determina dell’Osservatorio sulle Manifestazioni Sportive.

I biglietti per Lazio-Atalanta saranno in vendita dalle 11 di martedì 24 novembre. Secondo quanto riportato da Sslazio, La partita di Serie A Enilive si giocherà domenica 6 dicembre alle 15, come comunica la S.S. Lazio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that le tariffe agevolate per invalidi al 100% e persone disabili in carrozzella, entrambe con accompagnatore, sono acquistabili soltanto nei negozi Lazio Style 1900, escluso quello di Parco Leonardo. La stessa modalità è prevista per i biglietti ridotti riservati agli invalidi civili al 100% e per la Tribuna Tevere non deambulanti, in entrambi i casi con accompagnatore.

Chi possiede una Fidelity Card Millenovecento o Eagle e non è abbonato può chiedere, anche durante l’acquisto online, che il titolo d’ingresso sia caricato elettronicamente sulla tessera. Ai biglietti acquistati online si applica una commissione di servizio del 3,80%.

According to recent reports, il biglietto Ridotto Under 16 è disponibile per i ragazzi nati dal 1° gennaio 2010. I ragazzi nati dal 1° gennaio 2012 possono invece accedere gratuitamente allo stadio se accompagnati da un genitore, o da un parente entro il quarto grado, in possesso di un biglietto a pagamento.

Per l’Omaggio Under 14, il tagliando nominativo gratuito va ritirato contemporaneamente all’acquisto del biglietto dell’adulto. L’operazione si effettua esclusivamente nei Lazio Style 1900, tranne Parco Leonardo, oppure, soltanto il giorno della gara, alla biglietteria di Via Nigra. La Lazio mette a disposizione le indicazioni per gli omaggi Under 14.

I bambini di quattro anni nati dal 1° gennaio 2022 entrano gratuitamente e senza biglietto, presentando un documento d’identità o la tessera sanitaria.

It has been revealed that emre Mor ha deciso di sospendere la propria carriera calcistica a tempo indeterminato. Il 29enne del NEC Nijmegen, arrivato in Olanda la scorsa estate, ha interrotto il rapporto con il club di comune accordo, lasciando comunque aperta la possibilità di un ritorno in campo qualora le sue condizioni fisiche dovessero consentirglielo.

It has been revealed that L’ex Borussia Dortmund ha spiegato la sua decisione attraverso un messaggio pubblicato sui social: "Da quando ero piccolo ho avuto un solo sogno: diventare un calciatore professionista. Ho sempre dato tutto per questo sport che amo così tanto. Ma a volte la vita ti costringe a prendere decisioni per le quali il cuore non è pronto". Mor ha poi aggiunto: "Sono arrivato al punto in cui devo ascoltare il mio corpo, rispettare i miei limiti e mettere il mio benessere al primo posto. Non so cosa mi riserverà il futuro, ma dentro di me mantengo la speranza di poter tornare un giorno sul campo".

Nato a Copenaghen, Mor era considerato uno dei giovani più promettenti del calcio europeo. Dopo l’esordio con il Nordsjaelland e l’Europeo 2016 con la Turchia, fu acquistato dal Borussia Dortmund. In seguito vestì le maglie di Celta Vigo, Galatasaray, Olympiakos, Karagumruk e Fenerbahçe, senza però riuscire a mantenere le aspettative iniziali. Con il NEC aveva collezionato sette presenze, un gol e un assist.

#141394. Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

The club’s newly introduced managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

Industry observers note that 'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but promptly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

Salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

In a recent development, they are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You can’t be yourself,’ notes Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

Like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady noted that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

Intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

City have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

He utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

The format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

In a recent development, ‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson claims, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

In a recent development, ‘You're having the same conversations again. It was like, "Hang on a minute. I've had this conversation before". The previous people knew about it. They have the footage from earlier seasons – so do your homework, like we all do with our jobs. It almost felt like a bit of a lack of respect at times.’.

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for an eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise cameras were rolling.

Former Sunderland boss Simon Grayson was unaware of their planned Netflix documentary and didn't grant the producers access to his inner sanctum.

Sources indicate that these are the challenges that Amazon face with United, somehow attempting to earn trust or forging relationships in a matter of months before they pack up and leave. The film crew will be seen as outsiders.

There is intrigue within the industry as to exactly how granular Amazon can go amid the United chaos and whether they use fly-on-the-wall cameras, as was the case with Arsenal (in 2021–22) and Tottenham (in 2019-20).

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for that eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise the cameras were rolling.

Recent findings suggest that unlike Mourinho, Pochettino – his predecessor, sacked in November 2019 – had banned them from his office. He was never keen on the idea of the documentary and hardly features in the series, his dismissal coming early in Episode One – a sign perhaps that the film-makers got little out of him.

It will be fascinating to see if they gain access to his inner sanctum at United.

The club have had to double their media commitments this season as a result of the streaming deal, although they have been reluctant to organise sitdown interviews with players, telling Amazon that they must establish their own rapport for those.

In a recent development, some clubs have been known to give their content away for free, with Sky Sports taking two seasons of Mission to Burnley without paying. The driving force behind those moves is to promote brands. Under Alan Pace’s premiership, Burnley are staring at potential relegation to League One.

In a recent development, vincent Kompany, then the Burnley manager, is understood to have been vexed at his portrayal as a hot-headed screamer. Brendan Rodgers cannot have been overly pleased with Being: Liverpool, which ended in public ridicule and comparisons to David Brent. Players at other clubs have confided that they hid from cameras.

‘You can’t be yourself, you never forget the cameras are there,’ states Grayson of his season alongside the makers of Sunderland 'Til I Die.

Salford's co-manager Anthony Johnson gives his players a dressing down in the BBC documentary.

Joey Barton, meanwhile, is still waiting for his moment – and may be for some time. Fleetwood Town commissioned their own team to chart his start in management and streaming giants Dazn purchased the rights.

In a recent development, it was so close to being aired that Fleetwood held a premiere at Highbury Stadium for 100 supporters including the local mayor, only for one of Barton’s brushes with law enforcement in the intervening days to suspend the broadcast. Prolonged legal proceedings meant the idea was canned and Dazn’s licencing period expired.

It has been revealed that it was later resurrected, focusing in part on then Fleetwood owner Andy Pilley’s fraud trial – a crew followed him into court on day one – but was then shelved when a guilty verdict was handed down. Cameras are following clubs up and down the EFL from Birmingham to Cambridge via Sheffield Wednesday.

Grayson, for his part, refused to share his drive home from training with the crew and now admits that the ultimately unfavourable edit may have been a result of him not giving the production company what they wanted.

In a recent development, ‘I did a presentation with the players with a flip chart and everybody thought it was an hour before kick-off of a league game,’ he states. ‘It was actually done at 11:30am before a pre-season game!

'That’s why I let them film it, because it was a pre-season game, and it had no real meaning. But they presented it in the doc as if it was before the first game of the season.

Sources indicate that 'Part of the severance when I was sacked was that I still needed to do some work for them. I did three different (choreographed) interviews in a London hotel with different shirts on after I’d been sacked, done as if they were filmed at the time.

‘People said, “You didn’t come across that passionate about the club when you were talking about it”. Well, why would you when you were filming in November after you’d already been sacked? We were talking about deadline day in one of them. I’d already done something on that in August.

‘I think they had sympathy with me, but also if they’d had more sympathy, they wouldn’t have even asked me to do it. I’ve spoken to managers since and they’ve gone, “F***ing hell, you did well to put up with that".'.

Grayson only ever watched four episodes back and has heard his successor, Chris Coleman, was also dealt a raw deal.

Fabian Delph leads a Manchester City inquest during an FA Cup defeat at Wigan - the only scene from the dressing room that made it into Amazon's documentary on the 2017-18 season.

According to recent reports, mauricio Pochettino banned cameras from his office in his final days at Tottenham. Will he do the same at Manchester United?

Industry observers note that by his own admission, Johnson enjoyed the process more than Grayson did. One ex-Salford player claimed that nothing was really cut from the show other than a fight on a team-bonding night out. It was authentic, no-holds barred.

Until the end of Johnson and Morley, that is.

Industry observers note that ‘We won the league and we ended up getting sacked anyway,’ Johnson indicates. ‘We went to meet Gary (Neville) and the board. We went upstairs in Hotel Football and a cameraman followed us. Obviously they knew what was going on. When we got to the room for the meeting, they wouldn't let the camera in.

Industry observers note that ‘I'm actually smiling thinking about it. The documentary followed me and Bern everywhere, eating food or whatever, and then when the day comes to sack us, they didn't want the camera in the room!

‘The conversation was fine in the room itself but I think the perception from the outside world looking in would've been: "What the f*** is that all about?”’.

Hansi Flick's blunt Real Madrid claim as Mourinho closes gap

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:38.
  • Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has insisted that he is not concerned by Real Madrid's progress under Jose Mourinho, although his comments have taken on added significance after the Spanish capital club drew level on points with their bitter rivals.
  • Speaking ahead of Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, Flick dismissed questions about Madrid's improvement and emphasised that Barcelona were focused entirely on maintaining their position at the top of the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:38.

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has insisted that he is not concerned by Real Madrid's progress under Jose Mourinho, although his comments have taken on added significance after the Spanish capital club drew level on points with their bitter rivals.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, Flick dismissed questions about Madrid's improvement and emphasised that Barcelona were focused entirely on maintaining their position at the top of the table. At the time of his press conference on Saturday, the Catalan giants held a three-point advantage over Mourinho's side.

However, that lead disappeared later in the evening when Real Madrid secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu. Carlos Espi's late winner lifted Los Blancos to 33 points, level with Barcelona, although Flick's team retain first place with a game in hand.

In a recent development, the sequence adds an intriguing dimension to Flick's remarks, made just hours before Madrid reduced the gap to zero. Barcelona now have an opportunity to restore their three-point advantage against Villarreal, but their manager's determination to ignore developments in the Spanish capital will be tested by an increasingly competitive title race.

Asked whether he had expected Real Madrid to improve so significantly under Mourinho, Flick declined to focus on the performances of Barcelona's biggest rivals.

"I don't care about Real Madrid. What they do is none of my business," the German mentioned during his pre-match press conference, as reported by Brazilian outlet Trivela.

He explained that Barcelona's previous meeting with Madrid was already behind them and that his immediate priority was Sunday's home fixture against Villarreal.

"We are three points ahead of them and we want to maintain that position," Flick added. "That's what matters to us, not what Real Madrid are doing or how well they are playing.".

Those comments were made before Madrid's victory over Celta and should not be interpreted as a response to Mourinho's latest result. Rather than criticising his Portuguese counterpart, Flick was attempting to shift attention towards Barcelona's own responsibilities in the title race.

The former Bayern Munich manager nevertheless acknowledged the improving standard of competition in La Liga, pointing to several teams capable of challenging the traditional dominance of Spain's two biggest clubs.

"There are also Atletico Madrid and Real Betis, who are having fantastic seasons. La Liga is very strong, that's the truth," he noted when discussing Madrid's progress.

Sources indicate that flick was particularly complimentary about Villarreal, describing their head coach Inigo as an exceptional young manager with a promising future. His praise reflected the importance he attaches to Barcelona's next opponents, who could complicate the Catalans' efforts to maintain their advantage over Real Madrid.

While Flick was preparing his players for Villarreal, Mourinho's team faced a difficult evening against Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu.

In a recent development, the visitors made an excellent start, taking the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes. Madrid then missed an opportunity to equalise before half time when Kylian Mbappe failed to convert a penalty, leaving the hosts facing the prospect of a damaging defeat.

Jude Bellingham eventually restored parity in the 66th minute, finishing from inside the penalty area after Mbappe had provided the final pass. Madrid continued to push for a winner and were rewarded when Espi struck in the closing stages, converting the rebound after his initial header had been saved.

The victory was particularly significant in the context of the title race. Mourinho's side had begun the weekend three points behind Barcelona, but their determination to recover from an early setback ensured that the leaders would enter Sunday's fixture without any points advantage.

Madrid have now collected 33 points from 13 league matches, while Barcelona have the same total after 12 games. Flick's men therefore remain in control of their own position, although they will need to overcome Villarreal to re-establish a three-point cushion.

Barcelona were already preparing for a demanding encounter against opponents capable of causing problems for the leading sides, with Flick facing several selection decisions ahead of the fixture. The Catalans are looking to record their 12th league victory of the campaign and preserve their position at the summit.

Sources indicate that flick's refusal to dwell on Madrid's progress is consistent with his emphasis on Barcelona's own performances. Yet Saturday's result has removed their immediate margin for error, giving Sunday's meeting with Villarreal additional importance.

Industry observers note that A victory would restore the three-point lead that Flick was referring to during his press conference. Anything less would leave Barcelona and Mourinho's Madrid separated by little or nothing at the top of La Liga heading into the next round of fixtures.

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:59.

Real Madrid striker Carlos Espi has emerged as Europe's most prolific substitute this season, with his latest match-winning intervention prompting Jose Mourinho to explain why the 21-year-old remains such an effective weapon from the bench.

In a recent development, the Spaniard scored the decisive goal in Saturday's 2-1 comeback victory over Celta Vigo, taking his tally to four goals in all competitions without making a single start. No substitute across Europe's five major leagues has scored more this season when domestic and European competitions are combined.

His remarkable efficiency has become increasingly important to Mourinho, whose side needed another late rescue act after falling behind at the Santiago Bernabeu. Yet despite Espi's growing influence, the Portuguese manager believes the forward's particular qualities are better suited to certain situations than to Madrid's usual starting system.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho praised his young striker's attitude and penalty-box instincts, while acknowledging that his current role presents an unusual challenge for a player consistently delivering decisive contributions.

Madrid's victory against Celta offered another demonstration of why Espi has become such a valuable alternative to Kylian Mbappe.

Industry observers note that the visitors took the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes, and Madrid's difficulties deepened when Mbappe fired a first-half penalty over the crossbar. Mourinho introduced Vinicius Junior after the interval, with the Brazilian helping transform the hosts' attacking performance.

In a recent development, vinicius initiated the move that allowed Jude Bellingham to equalise in the 66th minute, combining with Mbappe before the England midfielder finished from inside the penalty area. With the game still level heading into the closing stages, Espi delivered the decisive contribution.

The youngster attacked a Vinicius cross in the 85th minute and saw his header saved by Ionut Radu, but reacted quickest to the rebound to put Madrid ahead.

Recent findings suggest that it was his third winning goal in La Liga this season, following similarly decisive interventions against Espanyol in August and Elche in September. All three arrived after he had entered the pitch as a substitute, turning matches that were heading towards draws into victories.

Espi also scored during Madrid's dramatic 4-3 Champions League comeback against Roma in October, when Mourinho's side overturned a two-goal deficit in the closing minutes.

Industry observers note that those four goals have established the former Levante striker among Europe's most effective impact players, despite his limited opportunities. He has found the net with four of his six shots on target across those appearances, an extraordinary conversion rate that illustrates his ability to exploit the few chances he receives.

The £21m summer signing has already made a greater contribution than many might have anticipated when he arrived at the Bernabeu, particularly given the presence of Mbappe, Endrick and several other attacking options in Mourinho's squad.

His latest intervention also carried considerable significance in the title race. Madrid's victory moved them level with Barcelona on 33 points, although the Catalan club retained first place with a game in hand ahead of Sunday's encounter with Villarreal.

While Espi's scoring record could strengthen calls for a starting opportunity, Mourinho believes his effectiveness is closely connected to the circumstances in which he enters matches.

In a recent development, "Some players have specific characteristics," the Real Madrid coach explained after the Celta victory. "I don't want to say that Carlos won't start, or that Carlos can't play 90 minutes, because he can.".

Recent findings suggest that mourinho pointed to the difference between Madrid's usual attacking approach and Espi's more traditional centre-forward profile. His team generally favour combination play and attacking runs into space, whereas the Spaniard thrives when opponents retreat towards their own penalty area.

"He's a guy with great quality in the box, a guy who's good in the air, a guy who plays well with his back to goal," Mourinho added, praising the striker's movement towards both posts.

The manager believes Espi becomes particularly dangerous when Madrid sustain pressure against opponents defending deep, allowing him to attack crosses and second balls inside crowded penalty areas.

That explains why Mourinho has repeatedly introduced him during the closing stages of difficult matches, often accepting a less balanced formation to increase his team's attacking presence.

The Portuguese coach also addressed the possibility of partnering Espi with Mbappe from the start, explaining that such an arrangement would require the wide players to take on greater defensive responsibilities. With Madrid's current attacking personnel, he does not believe a conventional 4-4-2 would provide the necessary balance.

Nevertheless, Mourinho insisted that the forward's status is not permanent and expressed his desire to reward him with greater opportunities.

"Football history is full of players like him, and I believe he can be decisive without playing many minutes," he said.

The manager also praised Espi for accepting his role without demanding that Mbappe be dropped, describing a player who understands his position within the squad and is continuing to develop.

For his part, Espi appeared equally comfortable with that responsibility after Saturday's victory.

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 19:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 02:46 EST, 19 November 2026.

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed his stint with the Ukrainian national team for the failed doping test which cost him two years of his career and revealed how fighting his case personally cost him millions of pounds.

The Chelsea winger, who is now on loan with Tottenham Hotspur, has opened up for the first time since he returned to football in the summer when his suspension was suddenly lifted.

Recent findings suggest that it was in a two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel. While the title of the video mentions ‘suicidal thoughts’, Mudryk clarifies during the conversation that he did not consider committing suicide despite being in a dark place. ‘Kill myself – no, that’s not a way out,’ he said when asked that question.

But he did discuss how Chelsea broke the news of his failed test to him, whether they helped their £89million signing from Shakhtar Donetsk during his ban, his belief that the drug meldonium entered his system while he was in Ukraine, and why he is now with Tottenham. He further claimed that he has faced threats from gangsters, and admitted his dream is to someday win the Ballon d’Or.

On the Ukrainian national team and their federation, the Ukrainian Association of Football, Mudryk said: ‘I’ll be honest, it pretended to help. But in reality, there was no help. They created more problems than they solved. Especially when we needed help the most, they turned their backs on us.

'I just would like, for the future, everyone to understand that you can only rely on yourself.'.

Mykhailo Mudryk has spoken publicly for the first time about the doping case that cost him two years of his career.

Mudryk has criticised the Ukrainian Association of Football over their support during his case.

Daily Mail Sport contacted the Ukrainian Association of Football for comment.

According to recent reports, continuing, Mudryk said: ‘The UAF is afraid of being left to blame in this situation, and afraid of the criticism or whatever else might come raining down. Distancing themselves from their own player, not helping, pretending to help, and in the end, first they drag the case out for months without really helping the case in the end. But at least the UAF isn’t to blame.’.

Sources indicate that mudryk was handed an initial four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test, with his last appearance prior to that coming in November 2024 in the Conference League away at Heidenheim. He scored in that 2-0 win for Chelsea. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'. Mudryk appeared for Chelsea during their pre-season tour before joining Tottenham on loan.

On how and why he failed his test, Mudryk said: ‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It’s a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe.

‘This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that’s Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

It has been revealed that ‘I was at home and Chelsea’s management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you’ve returned a positive doping test and now you’re facing a ban.

It has been revealed that ‘You can’t believe it’s true. You can’t believe this is happening to you. If I’d ever taken anything anywhere, I’d have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

‘At least I’d have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that’s the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

Sources indicate that ‘Otherwise there’d be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don’t hear them.

Mudryk returned to action when his ban was lifted in August, with the winger revealing Xabi Alonso told him to get game time and that he was 'counting on him'.

The Ukrainian joined Tottenham on loan but has seen injury restrict his involvement to date.

‘At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you’re falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You’re flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don’t wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.’.

Industry observers note that mudryk revealed how ‘the figure is in the millions’ when asked about the lawyers fees which were needed to fight his case. He confirmed he paid for that himself, along with the personal trainers and massage therapists he used to maintain his fitness while suspended. However, Mudryk did add that Chelsea continued to pay his salary during his time out of football.

Il tempo passa, il mondo si evolve e il calcio moderno non è più come quello di una volta. Oggi ci sono le tournée all'estero, le ipotesi di un match di Serie A in un altro continente e i diritti tv che impongono un campionato spezzatino, con la giornata che inizia venerdì e termina di lunedì. Gli appassionati però non dimenticano ciò che è stato ed è per questo che la nuova fiction La Famiglia Panini - L'avventura delle figurine, andata in onda ieri sera, ha intrattenuto 3.635.000 spettatori.

L'obiettivo è quello di raccontare alla gente come sono nate le iconiche figurine. Ambientata tra gli anni Quaranta e il 1970, anno del Mondiale in Messico, la serie tratta della famiglia Panini, formata dalla madre Olga, il padre Antonio e otto figli, di cui 4 uomini e 4 donne, che viene trasferita dalla campagna alla città: rimasta vedova, a 41 anni la donna acquista la storica edicola a Modena per permettere a tutti di lavorare. Questo evento, insieme all'acquisizione a Milano da parte di due fratelli Panini delle vecchie figurine invendute delle edizioni Nannina, segna la svolta. Il successo avuto suggerì infatti di stamparle in proprio e nacquero così gli album.

Una passione che è divampata subito tra bambini, adolescenti, ma anche adulti perché è ormai forse uno degli ultimi ricordi rimasti di un'epoca diversa, in cui lo sport e i risultati erano al centro di tutto, ancora più del business e degli affari. I ragazzi a scuola si scambiano le figurine Panini, sfogliano le doppioni ripetendo "celo, manca" in base a quali hanno già attaccato nell'album e quali invece ancora non hanno collezionato. In fondo se c'è ancora un po' di romanticismo nel pallone, si deve anche a questo.
