💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:20 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Neymar's streak of rage continued this week as he erupted with an expletive rant at rival fans who were provoking him.
  • The Santos star, 34, raised hell at Coritiba fans following his side's 1-0 win over them on Wednesday, with the climax of the Brazilian season approaching.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:20 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 19 November 2026.

Neymar's streak of rage continued this week as he erupted with an expletive rant at rival fans who were provoking him.

The Santos star, 34, raised hell at Coritiba fans following his side's 1-0 win over them on Wednesday, with the climax of the Brazilian season approaching.

'Don't f*** around! You're going to Serie B, you idiots,' he shouted.

'Suck it! You have to respect me, respect me, you f****** small team.'.

It had been a frustrating day in fairness - Santos' team bus had broken down on the way, requiring the squad to change vehicles.

And this is not the first time Neymar has vented his spleen this season.

Neymar branded Coritiba a 'small f****** team' in a rant at rival supporters who taunted him.

Earlier this season, he was involved in a furious altercation with rival officials in the tunnel.

In August, he was involved in a furious altercation with Remo officials after Santos beat them in the last 16 of the Brazilian Cup.

The Brazilian football icon screamed inside the tunnel as he was drawn into a heated exchange with Remo's directors.

He repeatedly shouted the word 'eliminated' before taunting the rivals with a series of gestures at his dressing room's entrance.

Despite his bragging over other teams, it has been a distinctly average campaign for Santos so far.

Santos sit eighth in the Brazilian Serie A and, despite him telling Coritiba that they will go down, that looks unlikely with the southern side sat 13th out of 20 with four games to go, four points above the drop zone.

Meanwhile, while he mocked Remo over being eliminated from the cup, Santos went out in the quarter-finals 3-0 on aggregate to Palmeiras.

Neymar has had a fairly effective season personally, scoring 10 goals and recording eight assists in all competitions while captaining Santos.

It remains to be seen whether he will play beyond the end of his contract in December, but the club's chief executive, who happens to be Neymar's dad, certainly wants to extend his son's term.

'We know that in every transfer window, offers come in for him to leave. Yet Neymar always chooses to stay at Santos. What I'm anticipating is that, first and foremost, I need to keep Neymar happy. Do you understand?' he remarked.

According to recent reports, 'And if he's happy here, I can keep him here. So, look, down this final stretch, the work we've done to structure the squad and open up positive possibilities has given us the license to dream.'.

Neymar, who was widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of his generation during his time at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, returned to his boyhood club Santos from Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in January 2025.

His £200million move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain remains the most expensive transfer of all time.

In June he made his first appearance for Brazil since 2023 after rupturing his ACL and meniscus in his left knee.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:31.
  • Cardiff City square off against Preston North End on Tuesday evening looking for the win that will create further distance between themselves and the relegation zone.
  • At a time when the Bluebirds sit in 15th position in the Championship table, Preston remain bottom despite a two-match unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:31.

Cardiff City square off against Preston North End on Tuesday evening looking for the win that will create further distance between themselves and the relegation zone.

At a time when the Bluebirds sit in 15th position in the Championship table, Preston remain bottom despite a two-match unbeaten run.

After 15 goals featured in Cardiff's two matches before the international break, it was anyone's guess how they would perform against in-form Norwich City on Saturday.

Taking the lead at Carrow Road put the Bluebirds on the way to a statement victory, but Norwich battled back to earn a 2-1 win.

Nevertheless, Brian Barry-Murphy will continue to take the positives from having 18 points from their first 16 games since finishing second in last season's League One.

Although they remain with just two points from eight away contests, they remain unbeaten across the same amount of fixtures at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Twenty-one goals - the second-best return in home Championship games in 2026-27 - have been scored, with Cardiff posting four wins and four draws in South Wales.

Many felt that Preston could have been cut adrift at the bottom of the Championship table ahead of their game with Southampton on November 7.

Instead, Graham Alexander's side have impressively accumulated four points from a double-header of the Saints and West Ham United.

Not only did Preston record a 1-0 win over Southampton, they held West Ham to a 1-1 draw at the London Stadium on Saturday.

That result meant that Preston put together a two-match unbeaten streak in the Championship for the first time since April 11.

Despite the growing optimism at Deepdale, Preston are still six points behind 21st position.

Cardiff City Championship form:.

Preston North End Championship form:.

Joel Bagan should return at left-back for Cardiff after serving a one-match ban for five yellow cards.

David Turnbull, Cian Ashford and Joel Colwill are all in contention for recalls, with Barry-Murphy potentially rotating his Cardiff XI having gone 85 minutes without making a substitution versus Norwich.

Perry Ng and Gabriel Osho are expected to remain sidelined through injury, along with Dylan Lawlor and Calum Chambers.

With Andrija Vukcevic suffering an injury against West Ham, Brad Potts is expected to deputise at left wing-back.

Stanley Mills and Andrew Moran also sustained issues at the London Stadium, with Ed Nolan and Greg Docherty in line to feature in a much-changed lineup.

The likes of Lewis Gibson, Harry Clarke and Liam Gibbs are again expected to miss out.

Cardiff City possible starting lineup:.

Trott; Kpakio, Fish, Bielik, Bagan; Turnbull; Ashford, R Colwill, Moylan, Willock; Salech.

Preston North End possible starting lineup:.

Nicholls; Nolan, Lindsay, Hughes; Offiah, Thompson, Docherty, Potts; Devine, Lang, Small.

Sources indicate that after a draw at West Ham, Preston will travel to South Wales with the belief that they can pick up another positive result on their travels. However, Cardiff are a far more accomplished outfit on home territory than away, and we can only see a hard-earned win for the Bluebirds.

Industry News: West Brom can trust 23-year-old to bounce back from costly moment in Swansea draw, starting against Bolton Wanderers: Opinion

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Brom made it seven Championship games without defeat on Saturday as they drew 2-2 with Swansea City away from home.
  • After Rabby Nzingoula put the Baggies 2-1 up, Jayson Molumby was fouled from a set piece and the visitors were given a penalty.
  • The fluffed attempt was quickly followed by Elijah Just’s equaliser, and it prompted serious frustration towards Price.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Brom made it seven Championship games without defeat on Saturday as they drew 2-2 with Swansea City away from home. WBA went ahead on two occasions and were pegged back both times, but the most frustrating part of the tie was that they missed a gilt-edged chance to go 3-1 up.

After Rabby Nzingoula put the Baggies 2-1 up, Jayson Molumby was fouled from a set piece and the visitors were given a penalty. Isaac Price, who tapped home the opener, stepped up and saw his panenka attempt saved by Swans’ shot-stopper Lawrence Vigouroux.

The fluffed attempt was quickly followed by Elijah Just’s equaliser, and it prompted serious frustration towards Price. It proved to be a costly moment, but West Brom can rely on their star man to bounce back.

Price’s development has been fascinating to watch since joining West Brom. He played almost entirely in central positions in his youth career at Everton and he stayed there while at Standard Liege for the most part, occasionally filling in as a right wing-back.

In a recent development, however, since joining West Brom, Price has become a true goalscoring attacking midfielder. He initially played in a central role as a No. 10, but in 2026 he has locked down a place on the left wing, and the 23-year-old has become a dependable goal threat.

Sources indicate that not only that, but the level of confidence Price is playing with for Albion has brought flair to his game. He isn’t opposed to taking on his man with quick footwork, improvising with a flick, or attempting a panenka penalty.

Recent findings suggest that the WBA star produced a brilliantly executed chipped spot-kick against Blackburn Rovers. Some may argue that it was foolish of Price to attempt another just weeks later, and they’d be right in hindsight. However, the audacity to try back-to-back panenka penalties is part of being a flair player, and it emphasises the freedom and confidence he is playing with.

Was that confidence misplaced on Saturday? Perhaps. But if it had come off, there’s no doubt that Albion fans and pundits alike would be lauding the cheek of Price for pulling off such a finish once again.

Sources indicate that price will be determined to bounce back from Saturday’s penalty miss, and there’s no reason to doubt that he can. The West Brom star has been in fantastic form this season, and he has arguably become one of their most crucial players.

Despite the miss, Price now has three goals and an assist in his last three Championship games. He can be trusted to deliver goals from the left-hand side and plays a crucial role in build-up play, as his technical ability from his previous time as a central midfielder helps him play incisive passes and maintain control of the ball.

Recent findings suggest that WBA face Bolton Wanderers on Wednesday night, and Price can produce an instant response to his Swansea City mishap. The Trotters play on the front foot and there will be gaps in behind for the Baggies’ attackers to exploit.

It has been revealed that price will likely match up against right-back Luca Stephenson, who is a dependable and energetic player. He has been booked four times in seven games though, so he could be worth targeting in one-on-ones.

Gabriele Borsa is a name that AC Milan will hope to hear more of in the coming years, and those years have now been secured.

Earlier this year, Gerry Cardinale admitted that he wanted to prioritise pathways from the academy to the first team, even with looks to invest more. Indeed, after the failure to re-sign Mattia Liberali, he’s been focused on ensuring they remain in control of the stars of tomorrow.

According to recent reports, so, the news of a renewal for Alphadjo Cisse is not a shock, nor is it shocking that Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto were given first-team deals in the summer. Whilst Borsa isn’t there yet, he hopefully will be one day.

According to recent reports, milan have done fantastically with Borsa, though. As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the 16-year-old has already signed his first professional deal with the club – posing in front of the Futuro logo – and this may seem like just another renewal.

Recent findings suggest that however, he’s an investment for the future. The Rossoneri believe he’s one of the best prospects in the academy and they want to take a chance on him and they weren’t the only ones. In fact, Manchester City had been sniffing around, but they’ve been pushed back by this renewal.

A ‘modest striker who lives for goals‘, Borsa is certainly one for the future and the jump to the Futuro will hopefully be another easy step for him. Importantly, he’s not another Francesco Camarda and he will be given the time to find his feet.

With consistent goals – which come in all manners already – he’ll learn with the Futuro and probably struggle occasionally. With Sergio Navarro’s guidance, though, he could become special.

Wolverhampton Wanderers vs Derby County - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:42.
  • Wolverhampton Wanderers will be looking to extend a seven-match unbeaten streak when they play host to Derby County on Tuesday night.
  • While Wolves are in third position in the Championship table, the Rams are in 22nd and at risk of being cut adrift from safety.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:42.

Wolverhampton Wanderers will be looking to extend a seven-match unbeaten streak when they play host to Derby County on Tuesday night.

While Wolves are in third position in the Championship table, the Rams are in 22nd and at risk of being cut adrift from safety.

Despite their dominance against Charlton Athletic on Saturday, Wolves only recording a 2-1 win has left Cesar Peixoto and his players open to criticism.

That is despite Wolves having now accumulated 17 points across a seven-game period, ensuring that they remain within one point of leaders Middlesbrough.

In the absence of the injured Raul Jimenez, Wolves perhaps deserve more praise for scoring 28 goals in 16 games, yet they are squandering too many chances for their fanbase to feel that they are playing to their maximum.

Returning 15 goals from eight Molineux games is only the seventh-best home scoring record in the division, emphasising that they are missing a cutting edge to a certain degree.

At the same time, Wolves have not conceded more than once in any of their last seven Championship fixtures, a defensive record that could prove pivotal if it can be extended in the long term.

As far as Derby are concerned, John Eustace may have felt that the 3-1 victory over Bolton Wanderers before the November international kept him in a job.

Losing 2-0 at Southampton on Saturday did not come as a surprise, and the Rams have remained five points adrift of 21st place.

Derby now possess the worst defensive record in the division, conceding 32 goals in 16 games and not keeping a clean sheet since a 2-0 win at Portsmouth on September 1.

A total of five points have come from their eight away games, with draws having also been earned at Burnley and Sheffield United.

Wolverhampton Wanderers Championship form:.

Derby County Championship form:.

With Peixoto again expected to rotate his Wolves XI, Jackson Tchatchoua, Nasser Djiga and Marshall Munetsi are all options to come into the team.

If Rodrigo Gomes has recovered from illness, the Portuguese may replace either Mateus Mane or Rafiki Stated on the flank.

After coming through 20 minutes against Charlton after a recent hamstring injury, Jordan James also comes into contention for a start.

Oscar Fraulo and Filip Bilbija could be drafted into the Derby midfield and attack.

While the Rams remain with Sammie Szmodics, Eiran Cashin and Ryan Hedges are both pushing for a return to the squad after injury.

Henrik Meister has joined the treatment room with an matter picked up as a substitute at Southampton.

Wolverhampton Wanderers possible starting lineup:.

Sa; Tchatchoua, Mosquera, Krejci, H Bueno; Andre, Munetsi; Mane, Lopez, Mentioned; Armstrong.

Derby County possible starting lineup:.

Widell-Zetterstrom; Nyambe, Duffy, Sanderson, Robinson; Mowatt, Fraulo; Brewster, Clark, Bilbija; Morris.

In a recent development, derby have shown signs of improvement of late and we do not anticipate this being a comfortable match for Wolves. Nevertheless, Peixoto's side are regularly finding ways to win matches without playing to their potential, leading us to predict a hard-earned victory for the West Midlands club.

Breaking: Man City owners see £1.5bn loan deal scrapped after lenders pull plug following Premier League charges verdict

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (642 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:59 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.
  • The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:59 EST, 19 November 2026.

One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.

Sources indicate that it was reported by Bloomberg last week that a German lender, Oldenburgische Landesbank (OL), had pulled out of a deal that would have let Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras take a large upfront payment against instalments City are due to pay them for midfielder Allan Elias, signed this summer for £32million with £2m add-ons. That bank views City as a reputational and financial risk.

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Apollo was in the final stages of negotiating the loan to City Football Group (CFG) in September, when the deal collapsed after the ruling that they artificially inflated their financial position to the tune of more than £900m over nine years.

City owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan injected £100m into the club in the month after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mansour, who has only been present at one City home game since Abu Dhabi bought the club in 2008, has made no public comment on the club’s conviction, which delivers huge reputational damage to his image-conscious country.

There are signs that football is preparing for a strong legal attack from Abu Dhabi if City lose their appeal. Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors in the event of sponsors Etihad and Etisalat suing them, it was also announced on Thursday. Legal indemnity will be in place for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and three other non-executive directors.

US private capital group Apollo Global Management abandoned a £1.5billion loan to Man City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

City owner Sheikh Mansou injected £100m into the club after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi.

But the refusal of credit by Apollo, which has loaned £80m to Premier League football club Nottingham Forest and has a minority stake in Championship side Wrexham, demonstrates that the capital markets think City are imperilled, with the appeal process by no means straightforward.

Recent findings suggest that if an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court. But to do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

In a recent development, financial analyst Paul Quinn wrote on The Esk website that Apollo’s problem had been with City, not Abu Dhabi itself. Three weeks ago, Apollo agreed to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. Apollo and City have not commented.

Quinn said that CFG needed the money because it was not self-funding, despite City’s financial strength. CFG’s pre-tax loss widened from £122.2m to £292.3m in the last financial year. City produced £694.1m of CFG’s £888m group revenue and ran up a £9m loss.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bradford City man Nick Powell has had an injury-plagued career and has opened up about how he considered retiring last January due to his constant setbacks.
  • On Saturday, Powell secured his first league start of the season and repaid Michael Duff‘s faith by scoring the opening goal in a 2-2 draw with Yorkshire rivals Doncaster Rovers.
  • In a recent development, the Bantams saw three points snatched from them after a 95th-minute equaliser by Sean Grehan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bradford City man Nick Powell has had an injury-plagued career and has opened up about how he considered retiring last January due to his constant setbacks. But the former Manchester United midfielder has stayed fit this season, and is reaping the rewards for his availability.

On Saturday, Powell secured his first league start of the season and repaid Michael Duff‘s faith by scoring the opening goal in a 2-2 draw with Yorkshire rivals Doncaster Rovers.

In a recent development, the Bantams saw three points snatched from them after a 95th-minute equaliser by Sean Grehan. Despite the disappointing end to the clash, there were positives to take for the hosts, with Powell’s performance and start being one of them.

Sources indicate that bradford City boss Duff spoke highly of Powell post-match, acknowledging that it was a risk to start him before highlighting his importance to the side. As quoted by the Yorkshire Post, he remarked:.

Sources indicate that “It was his first league start (this season), and he’s been here a long time. It was always a risk. There are lengthy conversations from a psychological and a physical point of view, which him, the physios, the sports scientists and myself are all involved in, because he can do things that other players at this level can’t.

It has been revealed that “Nick’s missed a lot of football in his career and he’s now in his later years and it looks like he’s enjoying being out on the pitch. The only reason he’s played at this level is because of his body, his injury history. He’s influential in the group. They look up to him because none of our other players and staff have ever been at Man United.”.

The midfielder-turned-striker has found his feet this season at Valley Parade and is growing in confidence, week by week. His injury record has hampered his chances of breaking into the City starting squad sooner, but right now, the No. 9 spot is his to lose.

The 32-year-old is in a rich vein of form right now, scoring four and assisting one in his last three appearances.

Nobody has ever doubted Powell’s ability on a football pitch, whether that was him playing in the Premier League or when he was playing in League Two. But, the one thing that has held him back in his career is injuries.

Right now though, the Crewe-born man has strung a healthy run of games together, and to go with that, plenty of positive performances too.

Powell’s manager and Bradford City teammates all speak so highly of him and how vital he is to the squad both on and off the pitch. His wealth of experience playing in higher divisions is crucial for the Bantams as they look to secure promotion to the Championship this season.

According to recent reports, if Powell can continue his great run of form and maintain his availability during the busiest period of the season, then he will only grow in confidence regarding his body. Even though we are only in November, he has already played in more games this season than in any of the previous two campaigns in the league, with 12 appearances.

Sources indicate that the Bantams are in a tricky spot right now when it comes to league form, having won just one of their last seven. But Powell has been a shining light for Bradford in what has been a difficult run of results.

Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund: Head-to-head record and past meetings

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (472 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 11:57, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 16:25.
  • Separated by just one point but nine places in the Champions League rankings, Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund cross paths in Tuesday's league-phase encounter at the Emirates Stadium.
  • The Gunners boast a marginal advantage over their German counterparts, having taken 10 points from their opening four fixtures against Napoli, Bayern Munich, Lille and Slavia Prague.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 11:57, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 16:25.

Separated by just one point but nine places in the Champions League rankings, Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund cross paths in Tuesday's league-phase encounter at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners boast a marginal advantage over their German counterparts, having taken 10 points from their opening four fixtures against Napoli, Bayern Munich, Lille and Slavia Prague.

Meanwhile, Niko Kovac has guided Dortmund to victories over Real Betis, Sabah FK and Villarreal, albeit while also overseeing a dampening 1-0 defeat away to Bodo/Glimt on matchday two.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

From eight previous Champions League meetings between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund, the North London giants hold the bragging rights, but only just.

Indeed, the Gunners have won four of their eight head-to-heads compared to three for BVB, while only one previous encounter has ended all square.

The 2002-03 season marked the inaugural competitive meetings between Arsenal and Dortmund, who each got one over the other in the group stage; the Gunners triumphed 2-0 at Highbury as Dennis Bergkamp and Freddie Ljungberg netted in the second half, before Dortmund prevailed 2-1 at home, courtesy of a winner from future Arsenal fan favourite Tomas Rosicky.

Not until the 2011-12 season would the two teams butt heads again, but they were subsequently drawn to face each other in three of the next four Champions League group-stage campaigns.

Dortmund and Arsenal drew 1-1 at Signal Iduna Park in September 2011, but Arsene Wenger's men prevailed 2-1 at the Emirates two months later thanks to a Robin van Persie brace.

Both sides then beat each other away from home for the first time in the 2013-14 campaign, Dortmund earning a 2-1 Emirates triumph before Arsenal won 1-0 in Germany, Aaron Ramsey nodding home the only goal.

The 2014-15 campaign also saw Arsenal and Dortmund trade blows and victories, as Jurgen Klopp inspired BVB to a 2-0 success at the Westfalenstadion, before Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez sealed an identical Gunners win in North London.

Arteta captained Arsenal to victory in their November 2014 Emirates showdown, but that would prove to be the Spaniard's final senior appearance of that season, as he picked up a serious calf injury in the second half before also undergoing ankle surgery.

Nov 26, 2014: Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Sep 16, 2014: Borussia Dortmund 2-0 Arsenal (Champions League).

Nov 06, 2013: Borussia Dortmund 0-1 Arsenal (Champions League).

Oct 22, 2013: Arsenal 1-2 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Nov 23, 2011: Arsenal 2-1 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Sep 13, 2011: Borussia Dortmund 1-1 Arsenal (Champions League).

Oct 30, 2002: Borussia Dortmund 2-1 Arsenal (Champions League).

Sep 17, 2002: Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

#141253. 'If you don't give him what he wants, he'll burn your house down': Inside the 'cult' of Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as sources from his crumbling sporting empire reveal the destructive know-it-all arrogance of Man United co-owner and his henchmen

'If you don't give him what he wants, he'll burn your house down': Inside the 'cult' of Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as sources from his crumbling sporting empire reveal the destructive know-it-all arrogance of Man United co-owner and his henchmen

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 12:11 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that the flat rural acres of the Turweston Aerodrome, in the north-west corner of Buckinghamshire, are far enough from human habitation for anyone padlocked in a building out there to feel seriously threatened.
  • The ‘imprisonment’ of the four-time British Olympic champion in a building, with signs declaring ‘No Entry’ fixed to the external doors, was one of the more extraordinary allegations to emerge from the court case, settled this week, over a £180million yacht Ratcliffe and Ainslie built together for the 2024 America’s Cup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 12:11 EST, 19 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the flat rural acres of the Turweston Aerodrome, in the north-west corner of Buckinghamshire, are far enough from human habitation for anyone padlocked in a building out there to feel seriously threatened. And if the testimony of Sir Ben Ainslie is to be believed, that’s what can come of crossing swords with Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The ‘imprisonment’ of the four-time British Olympic champion in a building, with signs declaring ‘No Entry’ fixed to the external doors, was one of the more extraordinary allegations to emerge from the court case, settled this week, over a £180million yacht Ratcliffe and Ainslie built together for the 2024 America’s Cup.

According to recent reports, ratcliffe, who had withdrawn financial support, was demanding the team’s assets and intellectual property, and, according to court papers, Ineos representative Raymond Fellows, assisted by two security contractors, arrived at the offices of Ainslie's Athena Racing and applied his own chain and padlock. He’d been refused the keys by the building’s owner. Ainslie and his financial officer Matt Robinson managed to leave the building through the fire escape.

Ineos were applying petrochemicals business methods to sport, as usual. Fellows had also been employed by Ratcliffe to provide security assistance amid protests at Ineos’ controversial British fracking sites. The experienced security industry executive observed that ‘a small hard core group of activists’ was at work and that social media surveillance was useful, according to court papers from an earlier case.

Ineos denied the ‘false imprisonment’ of Ainslie, insisting that their employee had padlocked the building to prevent anyone entering, not knowing that someone was inside and that, in any case, there were ‘alternative exit routes’.

According to recent reports, but the tech giant did not entirely challenge Ainslie’s claim that Rob Nevin, chairman of Ratcliffe’s sports division and a Manchester United board member, had told him during a heated meeting about the disputed boat in Barcelona: ‘We have a phrase at Ineos: scorched earth. It means that if you don’t give Jim what he wants, he will burn your house down, or words to that effect.’.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe's relationship with his one-time friend Ben Ainslie ruptured after Ineos withdrew support for the latter's America’s Cup bid.

Recent findings suggest that ratcliffe's running of Manchester United is criticised by one anonymous source. ‘People like him see football on TV and just assume they can do it,’ they say.

That threat, which Ineos say was only made figuratively, illustrates how Ratcliffe runs his businesses with what several sources describe as a cult-like authority, full of such maxims and mantras laid down to staff who fear him.

That ‘cult of Sir Jim’ is born of the billionaire’s own immense air of superiority and is something he seems to have instilled in some of his most senior executives.

Nevin, 68, a long-standing Ratcliffe lieutenant, has informed some who have encountered him since he arrived at Old Trafford that he has completed 60 or more major ‘transactions’ – business deals – in the oil and gas industry. He is described as ‘not short on confidence’.

Nevin chairs Ineos Sport, the collection of acquisitions built up when Ratcliffe believed his firm could straddle multiple sports and succeed at all of them, in the style of Red Bull. Ratcliffe disastrously installed his brother, Bob, as chief executive at OGC Nice, the second of the football teams he bought, and that air of superiority and ‘always knowing’ has been manifest at United, too.

Sources indicate that ratcliffe demonstrated to some of the Manchester United players the stretches he was using for London Marathon training, after buying the club. He considered his friend Sir Dave Brailsford to be ‘best in class’ when it came to running the football side of the club, despite the former Team Sky cycling chief only having a loose connection of football contacts, mostly picked up from his appearances on the Leaders in Sport conference circuit for his friend Jimmy Worrall, the entrepreneur who set up that business.

Sources have told us that Brailsford was so enamoured with Manchester City, after arriving to ‘save United’, that he and other Ineos people were ‘skipping around’ when Omar Berrada, chief operations officer at the Etihad, was hired as chief executive.

Sources indicate that ‘There was no sense from Ratcliffe of needing people who understand the industry and its craft,’ claims one source, speaking on condition of anonymity. ‘People like this see football on TV and just assume they can do it.’.

Ratcliffe (pictured next to former United boss Erik ten Hag) inexplicably considered Dave Brailsford (right) to be ‘best in class’ when it came to running the football side of the club.

Rob Nevin (right) chairs Ineos Sport, the collection of acquisitions built up when Ratcliffe wrongly believed his firm could straddle multiple sports and succeed at all of them.

According to recent reports, none of Ratcliffe’s executives will be wanting to tell him that. A further sense of what a formidable presence he is for his own staff came in a 30-minute ‘Ask Jim’ interview with him, conducted by his own director of corporate affairs, Tom Crotty, this summer.

Ratcliffe stares at the floor for much of the time as Crotty bowls him a series of long-hop questions and he seems profoundly miserable, revealing little more than his unhappiness with the British government’s management of North Sea oilfields and his dislike for the British sports press.

The interview was conducted the day after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina in July, which Ratcliffe attended. ‘It was fabulous. A great celebration, despite the whining British press who really didn’t like it,’ he notes.

In a recent development, asked how he switches off, he cites time on the golf driving range and fishing on his salmon farm in Iceland – to which Berrada and the Glazers have had to make their way for some executive meetings. ‘Biggest lessons learned in 2025?’ There don’t appear to have been any. At no stage do United feature.

Ratcliffe trots out his extremely well-worn mantra about the major three traits Ineos prize most – ‘Grit, rigour, humour’ – informing the relentlessly positive Crotty of the need to ‘do work properly before you make important decisions, because you need to spend capital well.’.

Sources indicate that that’s not happened in sport. The extraordinary rupture with Ainslie, after Ineos withdrew support for a third America’s Cup cycle and he continued to use the boat, is part of a general, hugely acrimonious winding down of the Ineos Sport masterplan.

OGC Nice and FC Lausanne-Sport, Ratcliffe’s European football clubs, are up for sale amid fan protest, while it is widely expected that Ineos will eventually disappear from cycling. They have already diluted their involvement, with the team formerly known as the Ineos Grenadiers now co-sponsored by Danish technology firm Netcompany. The All Blacks and Tottenham Hotspur both sued Ineos for prematurely terminating commercial relationships. Both parties ultimately reached a confidential legal settlement with the company.

What United need, as they look to Mauricio Pochettino for deliverance, is for Ratcliffe to climb down from his lofty peak, display some of the humility which has been missing and admit there have been faults.

What United need, as they look to Mauricio Pochettino for deliverance, is for Ratcliffe to display some humility.

The club's executives, including CEO Omar Berrada (centre) and director of football Jason Wilcox (right), have appeared out of their depth and in need of support.

Industry observers note that the view among some outsiders who interact at a high level with the club is, in the words of one, that United are ‘the biggest club in the world and yet no longer the biggest club in the world'. They carry huge expectation, yet are unable to compete for transfer fees and wages with Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City, and have removed excellent staff without replacing them. To cite only one, Victoria Timpson secured the club’s lucrative Snapdragon sponsorship deal but still departed.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If United were an iPhone, someone would need to unfold the paper clip pretty quick, push it in the side of the phone and hard restart everything,’ says the aforementioned source. 'The club need a genuinely industry-leading chief executive, a sporting director of the calibre of Edwin van der Sar who, unlike Jason Wilcox, has the experience, pedigree and knowledge he accumulated as CEO at Ajax. They need a boardroom presence and link to the fans like Bryan Robson.'.

Ratcliffe does not even sit on the United board himself, leaving it to Nevin and John Reece, one of the Ineos co-founders.

Another of his Ineos appointees was the 63-year-old Frenchman Jean-Claude Blanc, an experienced statesman and marketeer with an Olympic, Tour de France and PSG background, who is described as pleasant and without ego – though he was supposedly in the room when the 'scorched' earth comment was made to Ainslie. Blanc was recruited for his gravitas, rather than to pull up trees. He has stepped down from United's board.

Industry observers note that ainslie and Ratcliffe are no longer thought to be friends. Shortly before the alleged episode in the locked aerodrome building, Ainslie observed, in relation to Ratcliffe, that there was a difference between business and sport, where teams were delicately balanced, nuanced groups of people.

Industry observers note that ‘You want to save money and be efficient, but you’ve got to make sure you look after people. You need that balance,’ he remarked. Under the terms of the court settlement, Ainslie gets to keep the boat and sail off into the sunset, leaving Ratcliffe to whatever storms come next.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that QPR defeated Millwall on Saturday, winning 1-0 through a first-half goal from the returning Nicolas Madsen.
  • The Hoops make the quick turnaround to face Norwich City on Tuesday, and manager Julien Stephan has admitted skipper Dunne is unlikely to return for the Carrow Road trip.
  • In a recent development, in better news for QPR, full-back Tariq Lamptey has returned to training and is likely to be available despite also missing the Millwall win.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that QPR defeated Millwall on Saturday, winning 1-0 through a first-half goal from the returning Nicolas Madsen. However, one man who sat out was captain Jimmy Dunne, who picked up an ankle injury while away with the Republic of Ireland over the international break.

The Hoops make the quick turnaround to face Norwich City on Tuesday, and manager Julien Stephan has admitted skipper Dunne is unlikely to return for the Carrow Road trip. As quoted by West London Sport, he stated: “Not definitely, but probably not. It’s not a bad one. I don’t know exactly when he will be able to come back. He is still in a little bit of pain, so let’s see in the next days how the situation evolves.”.

In a recent development, in better news for QPR, full-back Tariq Lamptey has returned to training and is likely to be available despite also missing the Millwall win. The 26-year-old has been out with an ankle matter and last played in the 1-1 draw away at West Ham on October 9th.

According to recent reports, stephan has not been afraid to make changes and he is expected to shuffle the ranks for the trip to Norwich City on Tuesday night. Despite Dunne’s absence, he does still have room to make a change at centre-back if he wishes.

Recent findings suggest that ronnie Edwards captained QPR in the Millwall triumph, and he was partnered by Jake Clarke-Salter at centre-back on their way to a welcome clean sheet. The former Chelsea prospect will be the favourite to partner the stand-in skipper as a result.

But, if he wishes to make a switch, Stephan will have Liam Morrison to call upon. The 23-year-old is yet to make a competitive appearance this season and has been an unused substitute for 10 of the last 11 Championship matches.

According to recent reports, if one of the centre-backs was to drop out, it would likely be Clarke-Salter in order to manage his minutes. The 29-year-old has had injury problems over recent seasons but he has only missed two league matchday squads this term.

QPR don’t have the biggest senior squad in the Championship with 26 first-team players. However, they are well stocked in all areas and have already dealt with injuries this term, mainly in attack.

According to recent reports, stephan has shown a willingness to dip into the academy when needed as well. Leon Scarlett has emerged in the senior group, and 20-year-old midfielder Isak Alemayehu has appeared in matchday squads fairly regularly as well.

The Hoops have built the squad well over the past 18 months or so. The summer window saw them boost revamp their options at full-back and in goal, and there’s a balanced and well-rounded squad at Stephan’s disposal as a result.

It means he has room to make changes and ample cover when injuries hit.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.
  • The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League revealed updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The latest dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool at the moment have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

#141238. Industry News: Aberdeen's fresh manager is a proven overachiever with a massive personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1345 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Aberdeen's fresh manager is a proven overachiever with a massive personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1345 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event. While unquestionably a successful manager with Motherwell and St Mirren, there was always a lingering doubt about whether his skill set would work at a bigger club with different expectations in terms of style of play. And so it proved.

What didn’t help the Northern Irishman was the perception that those who employed him weren’t exactly bowled over by him in the first place, either.

Robinson would have been a hard enough sell to the Dons support had he been unveiled a few days after Jimmy Thelin departed the scene in January.

That it took them 67 days to deliver confirmation of the appointment – after the club had dalliances with Eirik Horneland and Sandro Schwarz – was hardly a ringing endorsement of their faith in him.

In a recent development, the contrast with the process to appoint Mario Frick is striking. Robinson was sacked two days after a four-goal home thrashing by Hibernian. Five days later, the former Liechtenstein international was named by the Pittodrie club as the new head coach.

Sources indicate that after the saga at the start of the year which reflected well on no one, Aberdeen, to give them their dues, knew what they wanted and saw Frick as a hand-in-glove fit. So, what led them so promptly to his door?

Mario Frick is unveiled at Pittodrie and immediately vowed to transform the club's fortunes.

The 52-year-old, essentially, is a head coach who fits in with the overarching strategy Aberdeen identified several years ago.

This has been lost along the way as poor results have seen a churn of individuals occupy the dug-out, many of whom were square pegs in round holes. This, the club believe, has been why the recruitment has been so random and ineffective.

There’s been little joined-up thinking, as evidenced by the summer window which saw 15 players arrive, many of whom were sub-standard or clearly not part of Robinson’s blueprint.

The intention always was for the head coach to work in tandem with the sporting director and chief executive rather than independently of them.

While Frick will have a say on what players arrive and depart this January, the conversations around the identity of the team and what’s required to improve it will be three-way.

At Luzern, Frick was happy to trust the judgment of director of football Remo Meyer on such matters.

His willingness to forge the same relationship with Aberdeen’s sporting director, Lutz Pfannenstiel, was the light bulb moment for chief executive Adrian Bevington and chairman Dave Cormack.

Frick earned 125 caps for Liechtenstein and scored 16 goals for the European minnows.

In keeping with the much-vaunted ‘continental’ model, Pfannenstiel and head of recruitment Darren Mowbray will largely identify players to fit the system. Frick will then be tasked with making it all work.

The blueprint is for the squad to be closely aligned with the head coach’s needs rather than assembling the rag bag of players who’ve come in the three windows since Thelin won the Scottish Cup.

There’s much beyond Frick’s willingness to defer matters of player identification to others which caught the eye of the board, however.

Although very much a modern and forward-thinking coach, he’s vastly experienced in the game.

As a player, he turned out for Swiss clubs including St Gallen, Basel, Zurich and Grasshopper.

He became the first Liechtensteiner to play professionally in Italy with AC Arezzo before signing for Verona, Ternana and Siena.

Across 125 internationals, he became Liechtenstein’s all-time top scorer with 16 goals, including one against Scotland at Hampden in 2010, the infamous game which saw Stephen McManus ride to the rescue with a 90th-minute winner.

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington welcomes new manager Frick to Pittodrie.

Being the star man for an underdog may have had something to do with his upbringing. Frick’s father didn’t exactly encourage him to make it as he started out in the game.

According to recent reports, he once revealed in an interview: ‘He told me: ‘There are thousands of talents like you. You won’t make it.’.

His coaching journey began eight years ago with Vaduz, who he succeeded in getting promoted to the Swiss Super League via a play-off.

Sources indicate that appointed head coach of Luzern almost five years ago, he turned the side from relegation candidates into one capable of finishing fourth inside 18 months. There followed finishes of seventh, sixth and seventh place prior to an amicable parting of the ways when his contract expired in May.

Although Frick didn’t win anything, Luzern is not a club which is accustomed to doing so, with their last league title arriving in 1989.

Its supporters still strongly identified with him, though, and recognised that he often got more out of modest resources than he was entitled to.

They enjoyed his big personality – not scared to wind up opponents in the media and not shy at publicly calling out his own players when they didn’t live up to the standards he’d set.

Frick famously scored for Liechtenstein against Scotland in a 2-1 at Hampden in 2010.

When he left there at the end of last season, the supporters felt the loss of a passionate manager who wore his heart on his sleeve, had no time for egos and stopped at nothing to deliver success.

In the Granite City, he will call out anyone not giving their absolute all every moment they are in a red jersey. And unlike the diplomatic Thelin, the fireworks are likely to be seen in public.

If his time at Luzern proves prescient, those who resist or disrupt the dressing room will soon be moved on. Those who do their best by him will have nothing to fear, however.

As Italian football fan Fabio Baccarini will gladly attest, although tough and demanding, Frick is also renowned as being a loyal man with a huge heart.

Baccarini, from Reggio Emilia, became fascinated by Frick in the early 2000s while collecting Panini stickers due to the fact that he played for Liechtenstein, a tiny nation he struggled to pronounce.

He wrote so many letters to his various clubs, hoping to arrange a meeting, that Frick initially feared he might be a stalker.

When they first met in 2011 after a game between Liechtenstein and San Marino, the forward presented Baccarini with a signed shirt, gave him his email address and invited him to a match in Vaduz.

And so began an extraordinary friendship which saw Baccarini regularly drive 1,000km to support the minnows and become their de facto mascot.

Recent findings suggest that three years back, when Hibs travelled to Luzern in the Conference League, the Italian super-fan was unable to find a bed for the night. Frick ensured he got one in the team hotel at no cost.

The latest Pittodrie boss is just the latest to follow in the footsteps of the great Sir Alex Ferguson.

As heartwarming as such tales are, it was, of course, the metrics of on-field success which drew Aberdeen to him.

Frick’s willingness to give young players a chance – another criticism made of Robinson – was a tick against his name.

He’s handed top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career. He appointed Ardon Jashari, who played against Scotland on Monday, his Luzern captain at the age of 20.

According to recent reports, he does not appear to be wedded to a particular formation. He mostly played a 4-4-2 with a diamond at Luzern, but he’s very much a pragmatist.

When he takes his bow at Rugby Park on Saturday, he’ll select a system to suit the personnel rather than trying to shoehorn the players into a pre-ordained system.

With just two points separating their team from bottom-side Kilmarnock, how the Red Army could do with witnessing a Super Mario bounce.

#141234. Industry News: Arsenal face fresh £80m transfer threat as PSG consider January response to Desire Doue injury

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (926 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Arsenal face fresh £80m transfer threat as PSG consider January response to Desire Doue injury

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 12:11.
  • Arsenal could face a fresh complication in their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with Paris Saint-Germain reportedly considering whether to accelerate their interest in the Frenchman following Desire Doue's serious knee injury.
  • Industry observers note that the European champions were already among the clubs monitoring Kroupi ahead of the January transfer window, but their attacking situation has become considerably more difficult after Doue was stretchered off during Saturday's 3-2 Ligue 1 victory over Nice.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 12:11.

Arsenal could face a fresh complication in their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with Paris Saint-Germain reportedly considering whether to accelerate their interest in the Frenchman following Desire Doue's serious knee injury.

Industry observers note that the European champions were already among the clubs monitoring Kroupi ahead of the January transfer window, but their attacking situation has become considerably more difficult after Doue was stretchered off during Saturday's 3-2 Ligue 1 victory over Nice. PSG confirmed on Sunday that the 21-year-old has ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will undergo surgery before the end of November.

In a recent development, according to TEAMtalk transfer correspondent Graeme Bailey, PSG hold a strong interest in the Bournemouth attacker, who is also wanted by Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur. The French champions could now consider stepping up their pursuit, although no formal approach or offer has been reported.

Any attempt to secure the youngster's signature would present a substantial financial challenge. Bournemouth are understood to value Kroupi at upwards of £80m and have shown little willingness to entertain a mid-season departure, despite increasing attention from some of Europe's leading clubs.

Doue's confirmed ACL rupture has left Luis Enrique facing a potentially season-ending absence in a forward line already weakened by the loss of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

The France international had scored PSG's second goal against Nice before suffering the injury late in the first half. He required treatment on the pitch and was eventually carried off on a stretcher, with Ferran Torres replacing him and subsequently scoring the winning goal.

Luis Enrique warned after the match that the injury was serious, although he stressed that further medical examinations were needed to establish its precise nature.

Those concerns were confirmed on Sunday when PSG declared that Doue had suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. The club also confirmed that the forward would undergo surgery before the end of November.

Although PSG have not unveiled a definitive recovery timetable, the severity of the injury raises serious doubts about whether Doue will play again this season.

The setback follows Kvaratskhelia's ACL injury during PSG's Champions League victory over Barcelona in October, which has already deprived Enrique of another important attacking option.

Industry observers note that paris still possess considerable depth, with Ousmane Dembele, Torres, Manuel Akliouche and Mika Godts among the players available to the Spanish coach. Nevertheless, losing two influential attackers in relatively quick succession could alter the club's approach to the January window.

That is where Kroupi's situation becomes particularly interesting.

Bailey reports that PSG are admirers of the Bournemouth forward and that Doue's injury could encourage them to intensify an interest that existed well before Saturday's events.

In a recent development, kroupi would not necessarily represent a direct replacement for Doue. Although capable of operating across the attacking line, he is primarily a centre-forward, meaning any move would also reflect a broader decision about how Enrique wishes to reshape his available options.

Recent findings suggest that there is presently no indication that PSG have opened negotiations with Bournemouth or made Kroupi their preferred January target. The possibility of an accelerated approach remains dependent on the club's assessment of its attacking needs.

For Arsenal, the prospect of renewed PSG interest adds another dimension to an already complicated transfer pursuit.

Industry observers note that the Gunners have been following Kroupi's development for several months, while Tottenham have also been linked with the attacker. Barcelona and Bayern Munich are among the other European clubs reportedly keeping a close eye on his progress.

Kroupi's emergence has made him one of Bournemouth's most valuable assets. The former Lorient forward scored 13 Premier League goals last season and has since earned international recognition with France, strengthening his reputation as one of the country's most promising young attacking talents.

However, Bournemouth are under little pressure to sanction an immediate sale. Kroupi remains under contract until June 2030, and the Cherries are determined to benefit from his performances during the remainder of the campaign.

David Ornstein recently indicated in The Athletic that a January transfer was unlikely, with Bournemouth expected to be more receptive to offers next summer. The journalist also suggested that the player could favour a move abroad when the time comes to leave the Vitality Stadium.

That possibility represents a further concern for Arsenal, particularly given PSG's existing interest and Kroupi's connections with French football.

According to recent reports, the financial demands are equally significant. Bournemouth have been linked with an asking price of at least £80m, although other reports have suggested that an even larger offer could be required to secure an agreement.

Those figures reflect the club's negotiating position rather than a confirmed bid from any interested party.

Arsenal's previously reported difficulties in securing a January deal therefore remain relevant regardless of whether PSG decide to make their interest more concrete.

A significant offer from Paris could potentially change the competitive landscape, particularly if the French champions decide that their injury problems justify an expensive winter investment.

Sources indicate that yet Bournemouth's position is unlikely to soften simply because another club has suffered an attacking setback. Any January approach would have to overcome the same contractual and financial obstacles facing Arsenal and Tottenham.

For now, PSG's growing need for attacking cover provides a latest consideration in Kroupi's future, but the immediate question for all three interested clubs is whether Bournemouth can be persuaded to discuss a transfer before the summer.
